Hairstyle Ideas

Hairstyles

Home / Hairstyles

Browse hairstyle ideas organized however works best for you — by face shape, length, type, or audience.

Finding the right hairstyle usually means balancing a few things at once: your face shape, your hair's natural texture, how much time you want to spend styling day to day, and whatever look you're personally drawn to. None of these guides are meant to be prescriptive — think of them as a starting point to bring into a consultation, where a stylist can adapt any of these ideas to your specific hair rather than applying them exactly as written.

Each guide below covers a different way of thinking about hairstyles — by the shape of your face, by how short or long you're willing to go, or by audience-specific considerations like the vocabulary used in barbering versus general styling terms. If you're not sure where to start, face shape is usually the most useful entry point, since it applies regardless of your current length or texture and gives you a vocabulary to bring into any consultation, with any stylist, for any future cut.

How to Use These Guides Well

The most common mistake when researching a new hairstyle is collecting reference photos without thinking about how they'll translate to your own hair. A style that looks effortless in a photo might rely on a hair texture, density, or length very different from yours. Use these guides to understand the underlying logic of a style — why it works for certain face shapes or hair types — rather than just the finished look, and bring that understanding into your consultation alongside any photos you've collected.

Hairstyles Change With Hair Health

Keep in mind that a style's success also depends on your hair's current condition, not just its natural texture. Heavily damaged hair may not hold a style the way healthy hair of the same type would, which is one more reason our hair care guidesare worth pairing with these style guides — the healthier your hair, the more styles will actually work the way you expect them to.

Revisit as Your Hair Changes

Hair texture and thickness can shift over the years due to age, hormones, chemical processing, or simply growing it out after a long time short. A style that didn't suit you a few years ago might work beautifully now, and it's worth revisiting these guides periodically rather than assuming your options are fixed.

Combine These Guides for the Best Result

The most satisfying results usually come from reading more than one of these guides together — face shape plus hair type, for instance, rather than either alone — since a style that's technically flattering for your face but fights your natural texture every day rarely stays your favorite for long. Cross-reference before you commit to a big change.

Trends Will Keep Changing

What's trending will inevitably shift again, but the underlying principles in these guides — proportion, texture, and how a cut interacts with your specific features — stay useful regardless of whatever style is currently popular. Use trend-driven guides for inspiration, and the more foundational ones for lasting decisions.

Still Not Sure? Start With a Consultation

If you've read through several guides and still aren't sure what direction to take, that's a completely normal place to be — and it's exactly what a paid consultation, separate from the cut itself, is for. Many stylists offer a short consultation appointment specifically to talk through options before committing to a chair-side decision.

Bookmark This Page

Hairstyle preferences change more often than most other parts of a hair routine — new season, new haircut inspiration, a change in lifestyle. Bookmarking this hub, rather than a single style guide, means you'll always land somewhere useful the next time you're considering a change.
